TANAKA Koki
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal:
-To gain the basic skills needed in processes from finding problems to solutions.
-To understand phenomena, objectives, and events quantitatively and qualitatively.
-To be able to find characteristics and laws of phenomena, objectives, and events.
-To be able to deliver the above information to a third person intelligibly.
-To gain various basic skills to proceed smoothly with verification activities.
-To be able to have a picture of technology fields and engineers of discipline.
advice:
In this course, to achieve the above educational goals, the students will learn the basic skills required for verification and problem-solving processes.
This course will deal with characteristic things of the corresponding department.
One is that the students will learn the basic "data-handling skills" needed for data collection → organization → analysis→ hypothesis testing → visualization → reporting.
One is that the students will learn the basic skills of "PBL for science and technology" including the basic elements of processes from problem-finding to solution and verification activities.
For "data-handling skills", the students learn basic experimental operations and the analysis method for data obtained through neutralization titration.
For “PBL for science and technology", the students prepare an experimental workflow, analyze data, discuss results, and prepare reports through group activities. The objective of this course is to develop the experimental skills and reporting ability necessary to carry out activities in Basic Experiments and Practice in Bioscience and Chemistry (2nd year), Applied Chemistry Major Lab/Exercises (3rd year), Preparatory Seminar for Design Project III (3rd year), and Design Project III (4th year).
We will conduct safety training to explain the handling of experimental instruments and use of chemicals. It is important to check and understand the handling and the risk of chemicals by yourself prior to the experiments.

For “PBL for science and technology", the students prepare an experimental workflow, analyze data, discuss results, and prepare reports through group activities.
